commits.subject: core: TOSLightLock is a non-recursive pthread mutex on Delphi POSIX
commits.body:
On Delphi POSIX targets, TOSLightLock fell back to TRTLCriticalSection, which
mormot.core.os implements over TMonitor there, so it was reentrant: a second
TryLock() from the owning thread returned true, against the documented
non-recursive contract, and the "Exclusive locks" test failed with Delphi 13
on Linux x86_64 (assertion #2046, TOSLightLock).

TOSLightLock now calls pthread_mutex_init/lock/trylock/unlock/destroy from
Posix.Pthread with the default (non-recursive) attribute, as it already does
on BSD with FPC. The mutex is stored in an opaque 64-byte TPosixLightMutex,
large enough for pthread_mutex_t on Linux x86_64 (40 bytes) and Darwin (64
bytes), checked by an Assert in Init, so that the interface section does not
have to use Posix.SysTypes. Lock/TryLock/UnLock are not inlined on Delphi
POSIX, since Posix.Pthread is used by the implementation section only.

Windows and FPC are not affected.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: net: new mormot.net.server.win unit extracted from mormot.net.server (#737)
commits.body:
Pure move of the two http.sys sections of mormot.net.server.pas, "THttpApiServer
HTTP/1.1 Server Over Windows http.sys Module" and "THttpApiWebSocketServer Over
Windows http.sys Module", interface and implementation, into the new
mormot.net.server.win.pas unit. The {$ifdef USEWININET} guard now encloses the
whole unit, uses clause included, so it is a void unit on POSIX like
mormot.lib.winhttp and can be listed unconditionally in the Lazarus package.

One cross-unit access is adapted, without any change to mormot.net.server:
THttpApiServerRequest reaches the protected members of its server through its
existing api: THttpApiServer field instead of fServer (both are assigned the
same instance in THttpApiServer.DoExecute), in 20 lines of SendError,
SendResponse and ProcessRequest.

mormot.db.proxy, mormot.rest.http.server, test.net.proto and test.orm.network
add the new unit to their uses clause inside the USEHTTPSYS / USEWININET /
not ONLYUSEHTTPSOCKET guard they already use for the http.sys code; the Lazarus
package and test project list it; README, CLAUDE.md, FOLDER-DEPENDENCIES.md,
SAD chapter 3 and CHANGELOG.md are updated.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: net: new mormot.net.peercache unit extracted from mormot.net.server (#737)
commits.body:
Pure move of the "THttpPeerCache Local Peer-to-peer Cache" section of
mormot.net.server.pas, interface and implementation, together with the
initialization assert, into the new mormot.net.peercache.pas unit.
HttpRequestHash() and HttpRequestHashBase32() stay in mormot.net.server, at
the end of the "Shared Server-Side HTTP Process" section, since
THttpProxyServer in mormot.net.async calls them.

Two cross-unit accesses are adapted:
- THttpPeerCache.State reads the public CurrentProcess property instead of
  the protected fCurrentProcess field
- new public THttpServerSocketGeneric.SetProgressiveRequests() method, for
  internal use e.g. in mormot.net.peercache, instead of writing the protected
  fProgressiveRequests field

mormot.tools.mget, mget.dpr and test.net.proto add the new unit to their uses
clause; the Lazarus package and test project list it; README, CLAUDE.md,
FOLDER-DEPENDENCIES.md, SAD chapter 3 and CHANGELOG.md are updated.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: crypt: TDigestProcess.Parse() accepts a void parameter value
commits.body:
- e.g. the opaque="" sent in the WWW-Authenticate header of some IP cameras
  (seen on two Dahua models): Parse() returned false, so DigestClient()
  returned '' and THttpClientSocket.AuthorizeDigest() sent no Authorization
  header at all - the server kept answering 401
- a void quoted-string is a valid auth-param value (RFC 9110 5.6.4 and 11.2)
- DigestServerAuth() still rejects any void mandatory field of the client
- new regression tests with the two actual camera challenges
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: net: TPollAsyncSockets.ProcessRead() won't buffer more than ReadMaxBytes
commits.body:
- the recv() loop did append to fRd as long as each recv() filled its 32KB
  buffer, and called OnRead() only once a recv() returned less: when the
  client sends faster than the reading thread consumes, e.g. on the loopback
  or on a loaded server, the whole input was retrieved in memory before
  THttpAsyncServerConnection could stream it to OnBodyDownload, or check
  MaximumAllowedContentLength
- e.g. on aarch64 Linux loopback, a 16MB upload was received by a single
  OnRead() call; an endless chunked body to a server limited to 1MB got its
  413 only after 188MB were sent (RSS 353MB, now 413 after 7MB, RSS 10MB);
  a 300MB upload streamed to a TStream made the process RSS reach 562MB
  after 281MB were sent (now 8MB for the whole 300MB)
- the loop now also stops once ReadMaxBytes (1MB by default) have been
  received, then calls OnRead(): the remaining input stays in the socket
  buffer and is notified again, as already done after any short recv()
- new HttpReadMaxBytes regression test
